subject: math
title: Fractions, Decimals and Percents
seo_title: Grade 7 Fractions, Decimals and Percents Worksheets (Ontario Math): Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Convert between fractions, decimal numbers, and percents, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 fractions, decimals and percents worksheets for the Ontario curriculum: repeating decimals like 1/3 = 0.333…, negative fractions, percents over 100%, common equivalents such as 1/8 = 0.125 = 12.5%, and mental math to increase or decrease by a percent. 100 math questions with an answer key.
key_big: Fraction to decimal: divide (3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375). Decimal to percent: multiply by 100 (0.375 = 37.5%).
key_sub: Know the common equivalents: 1/2 = 50%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, 1/8 = 12.5%, 1/3 = 33.3…%. To change a number by a percent, find the percent first, then add or subtract it.
body_html:
Fractions and decimals

A fraction is a division: 38 means 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. If the denominator goes into 10, 100 or 1000, you can make an equivalent fraction instead: 720 = 35100 = 0.35.

Some divisions never end. The remainder keeps coming back, so the digits repeat. Write the repeating digits with a bar: 0.333… = 0.3.

Decimal to fraction

Write 0.45 as a fraction in simplest form.

0.45 = 45 hundredths = 45100. Divide the top and bottom by 5.

Answer: 920

Negative numbers

Write −34 as a decimal.

34 = 0.75. Keep the negative sign.

Answer: −0.75

Decimals and percents

Percent means out of 100. Decimal to percent: multiply by 100. Percent to decimal: divide by 100. 0.4 = 40%, 0.125 = 12.5%, 1.5 = 150%, 0.005 = 0.5%.

Fraction to percent

Write 1325 as a percent.

25 × 4 = 100, so 1325 = 52100.

Answer: 52%

Common equivalents

Know these by heart. They make many questions quick: 38 is 3 × 12.5% = 37.5%.

Increase

Increase 120 by 5%.

10% of 120 = 12, so 5% = 6. 120 + 6 = 126.

Answer: 126

Decrease

A $120 jacket is 15% off.

10% = $12 and 5% = $6, so 15% = $18. $120 − $18 = $102.

Answer: $102

faq.q: What do Grade 7 students learn about fractions, decimals and percents in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Grade 7 math curriculum, students convert between fractions, decimals and percents in different contexts, use common equivalents such as 1/8 = 0.125 = 12.5%, and use mental math to increase or decrease a number by 1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50% and 100%.

faq.q: How do you change a fraction to a percent?
faq.a: Divide the numerator by the denominator, then multiply by 100: 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 = 37.5%. If the denominator goes into 100, make an equivalent fraction instead: 13/25 = 52/100 = 52%.
It is a decimal whose digits repeat forever because the division never ends, such as 1/3 = 0.333…. It is written with a bar over the digits that repeat.

faq.q: How do you increase or decrease a number by a percent in your head?
faq.a: Find the percent first (10% is ÷ 10, 5% is half of 10%, 25% is ÷ 4, 1% is ÷ 100), then add it or subtract it. For example, $80 decreased by 25% is $80 − $20 = $60.

sets.title: Fractions and decimals, including negative and repeating decimals

items.q: Write 720 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 720 = 35100 = 0.35. 0.72 just writes the digits 7 and 20, and 0.7 would be 710.

items.q: Write 18 as a decimal.
items.e: Divide 1 by 8: 10 ÷ 8 = 1 R 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 R 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 18 = 0.125. 0.8 uses the denominator as the decimal, and 0.12 stops before the remainder is 0.

items.q: The division shows 3 ÷ 8. What is 38 as a decimal?
items.e: 30 ÷ 8 = 3 R 6, 60 ÷ 8 = 7 R 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.38 and 0.83 only use the digits of the fraction.

items.q: Write 114 as a decimal.
items.e: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 R 3, so 114 = 2 34. 34 = 0.75, so the answer is 2.75. 2.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.

items.q: Write 2 38 as a decimal.
items.e: The 2 wholes stay the same. 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. So 2 38 = 2.375.

items.q: Write 725 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 725 = 28100 = 0.28. 0.07 forgets to multiply the top by 4, and 0.32 adds 7 + 25.

items.q: Write 0.45 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.45 = 45 hundredths = 45100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 920. 4510 would be 4.5.

items.q: Write 0.125 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.125 has three decimal places, so it is 1251000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 18. 125100 would be 1.25.

items.q: Write 0.06 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.06 = 6 hundredths = 6100. Divide the top and bottom by 2: 350. 610 would be 0.6, and 61000 would be 0.006.

items.q: Write −34 as a decimal.
items.e: 34 = 0.75, and the sign stays the same: −34 = −0.75. 0.75 is positive, so it is on the other side of 0.

items.q: Write −25 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 = 410 = 0.4, so −25 = −0.4. −2.5 is 5 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write −0.8 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.8 = 810 = 45. Keep the negative sign: −0.8 = −45. −8100 would be −0.08.

items.q: Write 1.6 as a mixed number in simplest form.
items.e: 1.6 = 1 and 6 tenths = 1 610. Simplify 610: 1 35. 16100 would be 0.16.

items.q: The division shows 1 ÷ 3. What is 13 as a decimal?
items.e: 1 ÷ 3: 10 ÷ 3 = 3 R 1, and the remainder 1 keeps coming back, so the 3s never stop. 13 = 0.333…, also written 0.3 with a bar over the digit that repeats. 0.3 is only 310.

items.q: Write 23 as a decimal.
items.e: 2 ÷ 3: 20 ÷ 3 = 6 R 2, and the remainder 2 keeps coming back. 23 = 0.666… = 0.6. 1.5 is 3 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 56 as a decimal.
items.e: 5 ÷ 6: 50 ÷ 6 = 8 R 2, then 20 ÷ 6 = 3 R 2 again and again. Only the 3 repeats: 56 = 0.8333… = 0.83. 0.83 stops too early, and 1.2 is 6 ÷ 5.

items.q: Write 49 as a decimal.
items.e: 4 ÷ 9: 40 ÷ 9 = 4 R 4, and the remainder 4 keeps coming back. 49 = 0.444… = 0.4. 2.25 is 9 ÷ 4, the wrong way round.

items.q: The repeating decimal 0.16 means 0.1666… What digit is in the thousandths place?
items.e: The bar is over the 6 only, so 0.16 = 0.1666…: tenths 1, hundredths 6, thousandths 6, and the 6s keep going. 7 would come from rounding, but the number is not rounded.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.3?
items.e: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333…, so 0.3 = 13. 33100 = 0.33 and 310 = 0.3 both stop, so they are a little less.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.16? Divide to check.
items.e: 1 ÷ 6: 10 ÷ 6 = 1 R 4, then 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4 again and again, so 16 = 0.1666… = 0.16. The answer is 16. 116 = 0.0625 and 16100 = 0.16 stops.

sets.title: Decimals and percents, including 12.5%, 0.5% and over 100%

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 40 of the 100 squares are shaded. Percent means out of 100, so it is 40% = 0.4. 60% is the white part.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percent.
items.e: Multiply by 100: 0.4 × 100 = 40, so 0.4 = 40%. 0.4 is 4 tenths, not 4 hundredths, so it is not 4%.

items.q: Write 0.08 as a percent.
items.e: 0.08 = 8 hundredths = 8%. 80% would be 0.8.

items.q: Write 35% as a decimal.
items.e: Divide by 100: 35 ÷ 100 = 0.35. The digits move 2 places to the right.

items.q: Write 4% as a decimal.
items.e: 4% = 4 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the point: 0.04. 0.4 is 40%.

items.q: Write 70% as a decimal.
items.e: 70% = 70 hundredths = 7 tenths = 0.7. 0.07 is only 7%.

items.q: Write 0.65 as a percent.
items.e: 0.65 × 100 = 65, so 0.65 = 65%. Multiplying by 100 moves the digits 2 places to the left.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 = 0.60 = 35 = 60%. 6% is 0.06, only one tenth as much.

items.q: Write 0.125 as a percent.
Write 7.5% as a decimal.
Write 1.5 as a percent.
items.e: 1.5 × 100 = 150, so 1.5 = 150%. A number greater than 1 is more than 100%.

items.q: Write 2 as a percent.
Write 120% as a decimal.
items.e: 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2. More than 100% is more than 1 whole. 0.12 would be 12%.

items.q: Write 250% as a decimal.
items.e: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5. 250% means 2 and a half wholes. 0.25 would be 25%.

items.q: Each hundred grid is one whole. What percent is shaded?
items.e: One full grid is 100%, and the second grid has 45%. 100% + 45% = 145% = 1.45. 45% forgets the full grid.

items.q: Write 0.005 as a percent.
Write 0.025 as a percent.
Write 0.2% as a decimal.
items.e: 0.2 ÷ 100 = 0.002. 0.2% is less than 1%, so the decimal is less than 0.01. 0.2 would be 20%.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
Write 0.3 (0.333…) as a percent.
items.e: Multiply by 100: 0.333… × 100 = 33.333… So 0.3 = 33.3…%, which is 33 13%. The 3s after the point keep going.

items.q: Write 34 as a percent.
items.e: 34 = 75100 (multiply the top and bottom by 25) = 75%. 34% just writes the digits, and 25% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 710 as a percent.
items.e: 710 = 70100 = 70%. 7% would be 7100.

items.q: What percent of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 5 equal parts, so each part is 100% ÷ 5 = 20%. 2 parts are shaded: 2 × 20% = 40%. 20% counts only one part, and 60% is the white part.

items.q: Write 920 as a percent.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 920 = 45100 = 45%. 55% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 1325 as a percent.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 1325 = 52100 = 52%. 38% adds 13 + 25, and 48% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 60% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 60% = 60100. Divide the top and bottom by 20: 35. 6100 would be 6%, and 25 is 40%.

items.q: Write 85% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 85% = 85100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 1720. 320 is the 15% that is left.

items.q: Write 35% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 35% = 35100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 720. 35 just uses the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: Write 2% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 2% = 2100. Divide the top and bottom by 2: 150. 12 is 50%, 15 is 20% and 120 is 5%.

items.q: Write 4% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 4% = 4100. Divide the top and bottom by 4: 125. 14 is 25%, not 4%.

items.q: Write 2750 as a percent.
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so 2750 = 54100 = 54%. 27% forgets to multiply the top by 2, and 23% is 50 − 27.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 34?
items.e: 34 = 912 = 0.75 = 75%. 34% only writes the digits of the fraction.

items.q: Write 52 as a percent.
items.e: 52 = 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 wholes. 2.5 × 100 = 250%. A fraction greater than 1 is more than 100%.

items.q: Write 1 14 as a percent.
items.e: 1 14 = 1 + 14 = 100% + 25% = 125%. 114% writes the digits 1, 1 and 4.

items.q: Write 150% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 150% = 150100 = 1 50100. Simplify 50100 = 12: 1 12. 320 would be 15%.

items.q: What percent of the bar is shaded?
items.e: Each eighth is 100% ÷ 8 = 12.5%. 3 eighths: 3 × 12.5% = 37.5% (3 ÷ 8 = 0.375). 30% counts each part as 10%, but there are 8 parts, not 10. 62.5% is the white part.

items.q: Write 78 as a percent.
items.e: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875 = 87.5%. Or 7 × 12.5% = 87.5%. 12.5% is the one eighth that is left.

items.q: Write 12.5% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 12.5% = 0.125 = 1251000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 18. 125100 would be 125%.

items.q: Write 1200 as a percent.
items.e: 200 ÷ 2 = 100, so 1200 = 0.5100 = 0.5%, half of 1%. 5% would be 120.

items.q: Write 13 as a percent.
items.e: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333…, and 0.333… × 100 = 33.333… So 13 = 33.3…% = 33 13%. 30% would be 310, and 13% just writes the digits.

items.q: Complete: 12 = 0.5 = ?
items.e: 0.5 × 100 = 50, so 12 = 0.5 = 50%. 12% just writes the digits of the fraction.

items.q: Complete: 14 = 0.25 = ?
items.e: 0.25 = 25 hundredths = 25%. 40% uses the 4 in 14 as tenths.

items.q: Complete: 15 = ? = 20%
items.e: 20% = 20 hundredths = 0.2, and 15 = 210 = 0.2. 0.02 is only 2%.

items.q: Complete: 110 = 0.1 = ?
items.e: 0.1 = 10 hundredths = 10%. 1% would be 1100.

items.q: Which row shows the same number three ways?
items.e: 34 = 0.75 = 75%. The other rows write the digits of the fraction, or use the denominator as tenths. 34, 0.75, 75% is right.

items.q: 18 = 0.125. Use this to write 38 as a decimal.
items.e: 38 is 3 eighths: 3 × 0.125 = 0.375. 3.125 adds 3 + 0.125 instead of multiplying.

items.q: 18 = 12.5%. Use this to write 58 as a percent.
items.e: 58 is 5 eighths: 5 × 12.5% = 62.5%. 17.5% adds 12.5 + 5, and 37.5% is the 3 eighths that are left.

items.q: 120 = 0.05. Use this to write 320 as a decimal.
items.e: 3 × 0.05 = 0.15. 0.6 uses 3 × 0.2, which is 35, not 320.

items.q: 125 = 4%. Use this to write 725 as a percent.
The double number line is split into 5 equal parts. What fraction and percent are at the red dot?
items.e: Each part is 15 = 20%. The dot is 3 parts along: 35 and 60%. 30% counts each part as 10%, and 35% just writes the digits.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 18?
items.e: 18 = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125 = 12.5% = 216. 0.8 uses the denominator as the decimal; 0.8 is 45.

items.q: The double number line is split into 8 equal parts. What percent is at the red dot?
items.e: Each part is 18 = 12.5%. The dot is 5 parts along: 5 × 12.5% = 62.5%. 50% counts each part as 10%, and 80% is 8 tenths.

items.q: Which is closest to 13?
items.e: 13 = 0.333… 33% = 0.33 is only 0.003… away. 0.3 is 0.033… away, so 33% is closest.

items.q: 13 = 33.3…%. What is 23 as a percent?
items.e: 23 is twice 13: 2 × 33.3…% = 66.6…% = 66 23%. 60% would be 35.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.6 (0.666…)?
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666…, so 0.6 = 23. 610 and 66100 stop, so they are a little less.

items.q: 16 = 16.7% to the nearest tenth of a percent. What is 56 to the nearest tenth of a percent?
items.e: 56 = 5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333… = 83.333…% ≈ 83.3%. Or 100% − 16.7% = 83.3%. 16.7% is the sixth that is left.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
18, 0.2, 15%
items.e: Use decimals: 18 = 0.125, 15% = 0.150, 0.2 = 0.200. So 18, 15%, 0.2. 18 is not 0.8.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: As decimals: 0.400, 38 = 0.375, 35% = 0.350 and 0.385. The greatest is 0.4.

items.q: Write −0.125 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.125 = 18, a common equivalent. Keep the sign: −18. 18 is positive, and −180 would be −0.0125.

items.q: Which shows 2.5 as a mixed number and as a percent?
items.e: 2.5 = 2 and 5 tenths = 2 12. 2.5 × 100 = 250%. So 2 12 and 250%. 25% would be 0.25.

sets.title: Increase and decrease by a percent: mental math and word problems

items.q: Find 10% of 340 mentally.
items.e: 10% is 110. Divide by 10: 340 ÷ 10 = 34. 330 subtracts 10 instead of finding 10%.

items.q: Find 1% of 4500 mentally.
items.e: 1% is 1100. Divide by 100: 4500 ÷ 100 = 45. 450 is 10%.

items.q: Find 5% of 260 mentally.
Find 25% of 84 mentally.
items.e: 25% = 14. Divide by 4: 84 ÷ 4 = 21. 42 is 50%, and 59 is 84 − 25.

items.q: Increase 60 by 50%.
items.e: 50% of 60 is half of 60 = 30. Add it on: 60 + 30 = 90. 110 adds 50, and 120 is an increase of 100%.

items.q: Increase 45 by 100%.
items.e: 100% of 45 is all of 45. 45 + 45 = 90, so a 100% increase doubles the number. 145 adds 100.

items.q: Decrease 80 by 25%.
items.e: 25% of 80 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20. Take it away: 80 − 20 = 60. 55 subtracts 25, and 20 is only the amount taken off.

items.q: Decrease 400 by 1%.
Increase 120 by 5%.
items.e: 10% of 120 is 12, so 5% is 6. 120 + 6 = 126. 125 adds 5, and 132 is an increase of 10%.

items.q: Increase 24 000 by 10%.
A hockey stick costs $80. It is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 25% = 14, so split $80 into 4 equal parts of $20. Take 1 part off: $80 − $20 = $60. $20 is the discount, not the price, and $55 subtracts 25.

items.q: A winter jacket costs $120. It is 15% off. Find 10% and 5% to work out the sale price.
A town in Ontario has 18 000 people. The population grows by 5%. What is the new population?
A 500 g bag of trail mix now has 50% more for free. How much is in the new bag?
items.e: 50% of 500 g is half of 500 g = 250 g. 500 + 250 = 750 g. 550 g adds 50, and 1000 g would be 100% more.

items.q: A school has 640 students. 25% of them take the bus. How many students take the bus?
items.e: 25% = 14. 640 ÷ 4 = 160 students. 480 is the 75% who do not take the bus.

items.q: Mateo’s family has dinner at a restaurant. The bill is $64. They leave a 15% tip. How much is the tip?
items.e: 10% of $64 = $6.40, and 5% is half of that = $3.20. 15% = $6.40 + $3.20 = $9.60. $73.60 is the bill plus the tip, not the tip.

items.q: A canoe rental costs $45 a day. Next summer the price goes up by 10%. What will the new price be?
Jayden answers 21 of 25 questions correctly on a math test. What is his score as a percent?
items.e: 2125 = 84100 (multiply the top and bottom by 4) = 84%. 16% is the part he got wrong.

items.q: Last winter, 160 cm of snow fell in Ottawa. This winter there was 25% less snow. How much snow fell this winter?
items.e: 25% of 160 cm = 160 ÷ 4 = 40 cm. 160 − 40 = 120 cm. 135 cm subtracts 25, and 200 cm is 25% more.

items.q: A store raises the price of a $40 sweater by 50%. Later it puts the sweater on sale for 50% off the new price. What is the sale price?
items.e: 50% of $40 = $20, so the new price is $60. 50% of $60 = $30, so the sale price is $60 − $30 = $30. It is not $40: the 50% off is taken from $60, a bigger number.
